content:
Reflect \((1,3)\) across the \(x\)-axis to get \((1,-3)\). For any point \((x,0)\) on the \(x\)-axis,

\[
\sqrt{(x-1)^2+9} = \text{distance from }(x,0)\text{ to }(1,-3).
\]

So

\[
f(x)=\text{distance from }(x,0)\text{ to }(-2,1)+\text{distance from }(x,0)\text{ to }(1,-3).
\]

By the triangle inequality, this is at least the straight-line distance between \((-2,1)\) and \((1,-3)\):

\[
\sqrt{(1+2)^2+(-3-1)^2}=\sqrt{9+16}=5.
\]

Equality occurs when \((x,0)\) lies on the segment connecting \((-2,1)\) and \((1,-3)\), which crosses the \(x\)-axis.

\[
\boxed{5}
\]
